notes.contract: contracts/stable/BridgedStablecoinV3.sol, byte-identical to the Ethereum bridge's launch token (creation code keccak 0xe560441f37e247e387cebd23bb3dd798a29d34174a9fb19a4bb3877c6c721de7); only constructor arguments differ
notes.source: sourceChainId is the Stellar network id (sha256 of the network passphrase) as a uint256; sourceVault is the low 20 bytes of the vault's contract id; sourceRoute is the vault's route. All three come from the DEPLOYED vault: tools/signatario-stellar/pairing.py args prints them, pairing.py check verifies them and the mint-chain genesis after the deploy
notes.committee: the same 7 `l2-mint-signer` and 3 `l2-token-guardian` keys as bUSDC (EIP-712 binds the token address, so a signature for one token is not valid for another)
notes.vaultSection: the vault's signer and guardian sets as deployed, for pairing.py check
notes.limits: as bUSDC: T = 0 (every mint waits 12 h and is cancellable), bucket 10,000 a day, cap 100,000, minBurn 10
notes.router: contracts/stellar/StellarBurnRouter.sol is deployed after the token, with the token as its only argument; it has no power
notes.deployTool: tools/deploy-pontes/deploy_pontes.py validates an Ethereum vault on an Ethereum RPC and is NOT adapted to a Stellar source; the owner deploys with the arguments pairing.py prints (docs/STELLAR-BRIDGE-DEPLOY.md section 5)
